# About Me
I am a population geneticist interested in the genomic consequences of complex trait evolution and the ultimate mechanisms that drive it. My PhD dissertation investigates intragenomic conflict arising from the evolution of viviparous matrotrophy, a live-bearing reproductive strategy in which mothers provision offspring directly during gestation, in the livebearing fish family Poeciliidae. Alongside this work, I am interested in computational, statistical, and machine learning methods for analyzing large-scale genomic and phenotypic data.
